who: Stephen Azzi, historian of Canadian politics and Canadian-American relations at Carleton University, PhD Waterloo.

evidence.says: History department profile identifies Stephen Azzi as a professor cross-appointed in political management with a Waterloo PhD; his research includes Canadian economic and cultural nationalism, and he supervises history graduate students.
Authority identifies Stephen Azzi as the author of Walter Gordon and the Rise of Canadian Nationalism (1999), whose biographical note says he teaches history at Carleton University.

notes: Exact name, Carleton history affiliation, Waterloo doctorate and Canadian nationalism specialization support the match. The cited sources do not independently name Chiarello as his student or supply the PhD year.

who: Peter Bailey, historian of modern British social and cultural history at Manitoba, PhD British Columbia.

evidence.says: Faculty biography identifies Peter Bailey as emeritus professor of history at Manitoba, trained for his PhD at British Columbia, and author of Leisure and Class in Victorian England.
Authority identifies Peter Bailey, also Peter Cecil Bailey, as the author of Leisure and Class (1978), affiliated with Manitoba's history department.
The publisher's record for Bailey's 1989 article on British leisure historiography identifies his affiliation as the Department of History, University of Manitoba.

notes: The authority and faculty profile connect the same author, Manitoba appointment and British Columbia doctorate. Published affiliations in 1978 and 1989 fit the student's 1987 doctorate; direct supervision was not independently located.
